subject: gov.policy
name: Ministry of ICT Strategic Plan FY2025/26 to FY2029/30
milestone: Launched with Service Delivery Standards, 19 October 2025
position_end: Launched at the National ICT Innovation Hub in Nakawa alongside Service Delivery Standards, on a programme-based approach to planning and budgeting across the institutions implementing the digital transformation programme; priorities are digital infrastructure, access to government digital services, locally developed ICT solutions, policy coordination and public awareness
note: the plan document is not held and the account states no quantified target; the Service Delivery Standards were developed with the public service ministry and the planning authority

subject: gov.policy
name: National artificial intelligence strategy
milestone: Under development, stated 2026-09-10
position_end: A strategy is being developed aimed at building national capacity to develop, govern and benefit from artificial intelligence rather than depending on foreign systems, the science, technology and innovation minister said in an account reported 10 September 2026; he said the country must invest in data, computing infrastructure, energy, models, applications and skills, and made the remarks after a meeting in London.
note: no draft, publication date, budget, lead institution or consultation process is named; a ministerial statement of intent rather than an instrument

subject: gov.policy
name: National Broadband Policy 2018
milestone: Implementation review published with the ITU, January 2026
position_start: In force since September 2018 with no implementation review on the record
position_end: A review of the policy's implementation, prepared with the International Telecommunication Union, was published in January 2026 and proposes interventions; it rests on a situation analysis of the broadband ecosystem covering the sector's contribution to gross domestic product, mobile network coverage, internet pricing, local and global traffic and usage patterns, and Uganda's placing in tracked international indices. No successor policy has been adopted
note: the review's findings and its proposed interventions are not itemised in what is held, and no adoption or implementation decision on them is recorded

subject: gov.policy
name: National Data Strategy
milestone: Drafting confirmed by the ICT ministry's permanent secretary, 17 December 2025
position_start: Did not exist on the record
position_end: Under development by the ICT ministry with other ministries, departments and agencies, civil society and the private sector; the draft is framed round data as a national asset, policies and legal standards for collection, protection, sharing and use, investment in exchange infrastructure, priority use cases in public health, agriculture, financial inclusion and education, and data literacy. It is pre-approval, with no adoption date, text or gazette record on file
note: the account is the permanent secretary's own, and no draft text is held

subject: gov.policy
name: National green data centre strategy and guidelines
milestone: Published with the ITU, January 2026
position_end: Published with the International Telecommunication Union, addressing the environmental cost of data-centre growth alongside economic and technological competitiveness, and addressed to government, the private sector, international partners and local communities
note: it is the nearest dated instrument the base holds to a national data-storage strategy; no dedicated national cloud policy is on record

subject: gov.policy
name: NITA-U Strategic Plan FY2025/26 to FY2029/30
milestone: Launched in Kampala 16 June 2026
position_end: Six objectives with targets: e-government use 9.2% to 40%, UGHub coverage of agencies 37% to 73%, national data-centre utilisation 70% to 83%, public satisfaction with e-government services 22.2% to 35% and IT-law compliance 67% to 81% by FY2029/30, reported against quarterly
note: the plan document is not held; the authority's own release dates the launch to 16 June and a later account to 22 June, and nothing reconciles them

subject: gov.policy
name: UCC telecom taxation reform proposals
milestone: Device-tax paper stated ready for cabinet, 5 August 2026
position_end: Excise duty on data and airtime 12% to 5%, VAT on mobile data 18% to 14%, duty relief on entry-level 4G and 5G handsets; the ICT ministry states a device-tax-cut paper is ready for cabinet before the end of the quarter, and no measure is adopted
note: the study itself is not held

subject: gov.policy
name: Vision for a Digital Uganda 2040
milestone: Issued by the ICT ministry, September 2022
position_start: In force as the overarching digital-transformation framework, on pillars covering digital infrastructure and connectivity, digital services, cyber security, data protection and privacy, and digital skills
position_end: Unchanged and unreplaced. Both five-year plans issued inside the window - the ICT ministry's and the IT authority's - are written to align to it, so it is the frame the rest of the layer hangs off rather than an instrument that moved
note: the document states a 2040 horizon and no dated quantitative target the base can track

subject: gov.legislate
name: Access to Information Act 2005
milestone: Section 1(2)(b) held unconstitutional, 4 December 2025
position_start: In force since 2005 with the exemptions as enacted
position_end: Two rulings moved the statute's boundaries inside the window without amending it. The Constitutional Court held the exemption for pre-conclusion court records unconstitutional in December 2025, while upholding the judicial service commission's shortlisting discretion and the privilege of its communications. In August 2026 the High Court set aside an order compelling an examinations board to release a candidate's examination scripts to a rival, quashing a UGX 12,000,000 damages award and treating the scripts as personal data within the Act's privacy exemption
note: no amendment bill follows either ruling on the record, and no request-and-response statistics under the Act are held

subject: gov.legislate
name: Computer Misuse Act ss.11, 23, 26-29
milestone: Nullified by the Constitutional Court on quorum and vagueness grounds
position_start: In force and the state's main tools for prosecuting online speech (2025-08)
position_end: Struck down, together with Penal Code ss.162-163 on criminal libel
note: the movement stem records an instrument neutralised; the rights reading is the opposite

subject: gov.legislate
name: Digital lending platform regulation
milestone: Stated at a finance ministry and parliamentary committees retreat 2026-08-18
position_end: The microfinance minister told a Kampala retreat that government is moving to close regulatory gaps around digital lending platforms, set against financial inclusion of 81 per cent (2023) from 70 per cent (2009) and an 85 per cent target for 2028 under the second national financial inclusion strategy
note: a stated intention; no bill, instrument or timetable is held

subject: gov.legislate
name: Legal and regulatory framework for artificial intelligence
milestone: Assessed with the ITU, 2025
position_start: None; no statute or regulation addressing artificial intelligence
position_end: Still none. The ICT ministry's own landscape assessment, prepared with the International Telecommunication Union, records that the country has no legal or regulatory framework for artificial intelligence, and the strategy intended to precede one has been in draft throughout the window
note: the government's own landscape assessment with the ITU is what looked and found nothing; a searched and cited absence rather than an unexamined one, and the strategy intended to precede a framework is tracked separately

subject: gov.legislate
name: National Drug and Health Products Authority Act
milestone: Passed at third reading, 26 March 2026
position_start: Did not exist; the 1993 framework stood
position_end: Passed at third reading on 26 March 2026, replacing the 1993 framework and establishing an authority to regulate the manufacture, importation, exportation, distribution and use of drugs and health products, with provisions for a listing system and for controlled use of unapproved drugs in life-threatening situations. No commencement date, assent or gazette record is held
note: the traceability and listing provisions are the digital half; no system, supplier or timetable is named for them

subject: gov.legislate
name: National Information Technology Authority, Uganda Act 2009
milestone: Gazetted 31 July 2009
position_start: In force as the statute establishing the IT authority and its mandate over government information technology, including data sharing between agencies
position_end: Unchanged. It remains the enabling statute under which the exchange platform, the interoperability framework and the security framework are issued; no amendment or successor bill is on the record
note: interoperability rests on this Act and on subsidiary frameworks, not on a dedicated data-sharing statute

subject: gov.legislate
name: Protection of Sovereignty Bill, 2026
status: In development, enactment reported but unconfirmed
milestone: Bank of Uganda technical assessment to joint committees, 2026-04-27
position_end: Before joint parliamentary committees in April 2026; described as recently enacted on 2026-08-02, with no assent date, gazette notice or text held
note: caps foreign funding at 20,000 currency points, about UGX 400m a year, above which ministerial approval is required

subject: gov.legislate
name: Registration of Persons Act, Cap 332
milestone: In force since 26 March 2015
position_start: In force as the statute establishing the registration authority and the National Identification Register, and providing for registration of citizens and of legally resident foreign nationals
position_end: Unchanged. Two of its provisions were operationalised inside the window rather than amended: the mass renewal and registration exercise, and first issue of identification cards to legally resident foreign nationals in August 2026
note: the consolidated text is as at 26 March 2015; the base holds no later amendment

subject: gov.legislate
name: Startup Bill
note: named as a reform priority at an August 2026 validation workshop; the base carries no text, stage or timetable for it

subject: gov.legislate
name: Telecom-infrastructure vandalism enforcement
milestone: Government stated attacks are treated as economic sabotage, 2026-07-31
position_end: A five-year sentence for mast vandalism in Kibaale, USh23.6m of damage, and a one-year sentence for a SIM-registration breach
note: the SIM conviction was under the Regulation of Interception of Communications Regulations, 2024

subject: gov.legislate
name: UCC enforcement against unlicensed public Wi-Fi
milestone: Public notice of 2026-07-07 opening nationwide enforcement
position_end: Nationwide campaign under way; unlicensed operators told to regularise or cease; no count of operators actioned

subject: gov.legislate
name: UCC order suspending public internet
milestone: Directive text published in full, September 2026
position_end: Connectivity cut from 18:00 local (15:00 UTC) 2026-01-13 and restored 23:00 local (20:00 UTC) 2026-01-17 — 4 days 5 hours by measurement; UCC announced restoration from midnight 2026-01-18 with social media and OTT apps still blocked; full restoration announced 2026-01-26, 13 days after the order. The Uganda Law Society called it unlawful for want of a state of emergency; the directives were ordered tabled on 2026-03-10. The directive’s own terms reached the record in September 2026: made on the Inter-Agency Security Committee’s recommendation, it suspended public internet access, the sale and registration of new SIM cards and outbound data roaming to One Network Area countries across mobile, fibre, leased line, fixed wireless, microwave and satellite; ordered operators to disable mobile VPN services and to block any public bypass; required whitelisted access for a defined exclusion list covering national referral hospital systems, core banking and clearing, tax and government payment gateways, immigration, electoral commission portals, voter verification and result tabulation, utilities, air traffic control and railway signalling; required incident reporting within 30 minutes and 24/7 response teams; and required any operator unable to comply to shut down its entire internet infrastructure, on pain of fines or licence suspension
note: contradiction resolved 2026-08-09: a duration must name its endpoint. Four days measures order to measured restoration of connectivity, almost five days measures order to the UCC’s announced restoration at midnight on 18 January, and thirteen days measures order to full restoration including social media. The scanned directive has no text layer, but a newspaper republished it in full in September 2026, which is the text this row now states; no ruling in the Law Society suit is on file

subject: gov.legislate
name: Uganda Bureau of Statistics Act, Cap 310
milestone: In force since 1998
position_start: In force as the statute establishing the statistics bureau and the National Statistical System, and giving the bureau its coordination mandate
position_end: Unchanged. The mandate was reasserted rather than amended inside the window, the finance minister calling in August 2026 for stronger production and use of official statistics to guide planning, budgeting, policy and monitoring
note: the consolidated text is as at 31 December 2000; no later amendment is held

subject: gov.protect
name: Be a Cyber Hero child online-safety campaign
milestone: Launched in Kampala 2026-08-14 for three years
position_end: A three-year campaign on child online safety launched in Kampala, led by the ICT ministry with the communications regulator and a private partner; no budget, reach target or evaluation arrangement is published

subject: gov.protect
name: Beera Ku Guard awareness campaign
milestone: Six-month campaign launched 2025-12; targets of 70% of Ugandans reached and 1,000 controllers registered
position_end: Campaign run; no outcome published against either target as at 2026-08-06

subject: gov.protect
name: Data Protection and Privacy Act, Cap 97
milestone: Registration shortfall stated by the office's director 2026-08-18
position_start: One extraterritorial ruling issued, compliance untested (2025-07-18)
position_end: Five corrective orders implemented by a foreign controller with the appeal window expired unused and no fine, against a registration base in which only 14,697 data controllers and processors are compliant out of an estimated 50,000 entities that collect or process personal data — more than 35,000 unregistered — with the office pursuing defaulters through the courts, the criminal investigations directorate and the prosecutions directorate
note: the statute did not change; the 50,000 is the office's own estimate and no prosecution outcome is held

subject: gov.protect
name: Data Sharing Agreement under the health memorandum
milestone: Provided for at 2.5.2, still to be executed
position_end: Provided for in the memorandum and not on record as executed: capped at seven years from the memorandum's execution, five over its course and two for reporting, governed jointly by the Joint Health Steering Committee with the Government of Uganda as data owner, requiring prior written authorisation, and binding all data activities to the Data Protection and Privacy Act Cap 97 and the National Data Governance Framework; the State Department briefly posted a subset of the memoranda in March 2026, then removed access and published none of the related agreements, and a suit for their release was unresolved at 2026-04-02. A rights organisation's reading of the seven signed memoranda puts Uganda among five whose text requires unilateral sharing of specimens and pathogen-sequencing data, and all seven as requiring broad audit access
note: a specimen sharing agreement covering genetic sequence data of high-consequence pathogens during an outbreak is likewise provided for, effective for no more than five years, and is not on record as completed

subject: gov.protect
name: PDPO action on election-period personal-data processing
note: no decision, complaint or public statement on the 2026 electoral processing is held, as at 2026-07-30

subject: gov.protect
name: PDPO decision in AdLegal v WhatsApp and Meta
milestone: Compliance confirmed by PDPO letter of 2026-07-17
position_end: Five orders complied with inside the 90-day timelines; impact assessment, adequacy assessment, legitimate-interests assessment and a Uganda-specific privacy notice delivered; no appeal, no fine
note: the confirmation letter is correspondence and is not held

subject: gov.protect
name: PDPO orders against Google LLC
milestone: Decided 2025-07-18 with 30 days to register and file cross-border evidence
position_end: No record of registration, a data-protection officer contact or a transfer-framework filing as at 2026-08-06
note: the precedent travelled; the compliance step was never recorded

subject: gov.protect
name: Prosecutions for unlawful disclosure of personal data
milestone: Three men held over incidents reported in July 2026
position_end: Three men held at a Kampala station over alleged false news and unlawful obtaining or disclosure of personal data, on offences under the 2011 computer misuse statute as amended in 2022 carrying up to ten years; the posts, the data and the complainant are not disclosed

subject: gov.protect
name: Public grasp of data-protection principles
milestone: Figure cited at the awareness-campaign launch
position_end: 13.6% grasp data-protection principles (2025-12)
note: a newspaper editorial argues the identification number is being handed over on request to security guards and others with no lawful basis, which is the public-understanding problem stated as a lived one

subject: gov.protect
name: Revenue-authority demands for bank customer information
milestone: More than 1,000 compliance notices since June 2026, reported 2026-08-17
position_end: More than 1,000 compliance notices issued to taxpayers since June 2026, and a letter of 27 July 2026 to a commercial bank seeking customer bank statements for December 2020 to December 2025, the directors' personal identity information and the bank-client correspondence, against a 2025/26 collection target of Ush36 trillion, a target of Ush40 trillion for 2026/27 and a ten-month shortfall of Ush1.5 trillion
note: the demands are made under the Tax Procedures Code Act and are set by the paper against the Data Privacy and Protection Act 2019; the revenue authority was unavailable for comment by publication, and no determination by the data-protection office is held

subject: gov.regional
name: EAC Cross-Border Payment System Masterplan, Ugandan participation
milestone: Approved by the Monetary Affairs Committee, 14 May 2025
position_start: Did not exist as an approved plan
position_end: Approved by the Monetary Affairs Committee of partner-state central bank governors at its 28th ordinary meeting on 14 May 2025, on four pillars - policy and regulatory harmonisation, infrastructure development and modernisation including the regional payment system and a regional instant retail payment switch, financial market deepening, and capacity building - and supported in implementation by the regional digital integration project. The central bank chairs the technical working groups standing under it
note: the masterplan text is not held and no Ugandan implementation step or cost is stated here

subject: gov.regional
name: East African Community Customs Management (Amendment) Act 2025
milestone: Assented and published, 26 September 2025
position_start: The 2004 principal Act without express recognition of electronic records
position_end: Amends the 2004 principal Act across a series of sections, including recognition of electronic records in customs documentation, which is the legal basis paper-light processing through the customs system and the single window had been running on without
note: a Community statute applying directly in partner states; no Ugandan commencement or implementation step is recorded against it

subject: gov.regional
name: Harmonised EAC framework for AI and digital-finance regulation
milestone: Proposed by the Monetary Affairs Committee chair, Kampala; absent from the signed communique
position_end: A chair's position only, with no instrument, drafting mandate or date; a regional AI policy roadmap was floated in March 2026
sources: 2026-07-31-eac-central-bankers-single-currency-2031|2026-03-31 EAC moves to create unified AI Sovereignty bloc
note: the stated argument for acting regionally is regulatory arbitrage

subject: gov.regional
name: Treaty for the Establishment of the East African Community
milestone: Signed 30 November 1999, in force 7 July 2000
position_start: In force, binding cooperation and harmonisation in telecommunications and related legal and regulatory fields
position_end: Unchanged as the legal base. What moves under it is programme work rather than treaty text: a harmonised regional framework for artificial intelligence and digital-finance regulation, a regional artificial-intelligence policy roadmap, and the regional digital integration project
note: last amended 2007; the digital provisions are the Community's protocols and programmes rather than the treaty itself

subject: gov.regional
name: Uganda's seat on the ATU Administrative Council
milestone: Elected at CPL-26, Abuja, 2026-07-24, for a four-year term
position_end: One of 25 member states in the Eastern Africa group; Uganda's floor intervention was on implementation reporting under the Union's risk-management framework
note: the Council coordinates African positions on spectrum, cybersecurity, AI and data governance before the ITU

subject: gov.standards
name: Adoption of international artificial-intelligence standards
milestone: Notified to the WTO as working drafts, target June 2026
position_end: The standards body's January-June 2026 work plan, notified to the World Trade Organization under the technical barriers code, carries two international artificial-intelligence standards as working draft Uganda standards - the framework for artificial-intelligence systems using machine learning and the concepts and terminology standard - both approved as items in November 2024 with a council approval target of June 2026. Neither is recorded as adopted
note: a work-plan entry is an intention to adopt, not an adoption; the target date had passed at the close of this window with no adoption on file

subject: gov.standards
name: Declaration of compulsory standards, 2025 preliminary notice
milestone: Preliminary notice published under section 20, 16 December 2025
position_end: A preliminary notice was published under section 20 of the Act, the National Standards Council stating that it intends to recommend a set of standards for compulsory application, with 60 days for written objections and a right to be heard before any declaration. No standard on the list is recorded as declared compulsory
note: the notice is the proposal stage; a declaration requires a ministerial notice in the gazette, which the base does not hold

subject: gov.standards
name: e-Government Interoperability Framework Reference Architecture
milestone: Delivered under the enterprise-architecture consultancy, 9 September 2021
position_start: In force as the technical reference architecture under the interoperability framework, delivered September 2021
position_end: Unchanged. It remains the technical companion to the framework, providing a controlled vocabulary, architectural building blocks and a method for identifying interoperability standards; the renewed architecture and framework delivered in May 2026 are not held, so whether it has been superseded cannot be established
note: delivered as part of the government enterprise architecture consultancy

subject: gov.standards
name: Government Enterprise Architecture and e-GIF
milestone: Renewed architecture and interoperability framework delivered 2026-05-27
position_start: The 2021 architecture and framework at their five-year mark, renewal not begun (2025-08)
position_end: Renewed documents delivered with the e-Governance Academy and World Bank support; rollout not reported
note: neither renewed document is held

subject: gov.standards
name: ISO/IEC 27001 certification of government institutions
milestone: Procurement authority certified to ISO/IEC 27001:2022, June 2026
position_start: No government institution certified on the record
position_end: The public procurement authority became the first of the government institutions selected under the digital acceleration project's government network component to be certified to ISO/IEC 27001:2022, presented at a ceremony in June 2026. The ministry states the certification programme follows from the earlier national information security strategy, and that ISO/IEC 42001 is expected to guide artificial-intelligence governance next. How many institutions remain uncertified is not stated in what is held
note: the selected set is described only as ten institutions in the selector's own note and is not enumerated in the source

subject: gov.standards
name: National Monitoring and Evaluation System reporting quality
milestone: Indicator standardisation agreed 2026-08-26
position_end: the technology ministry to standardise information and communication technology indicators and definitions with the technology authority and the statistics bureau
note: the government's own statement about its central performance-data pipeline

subject: gov.standards
name: National standards body and the National Standards Council
milestone: Ministerial direction on certification turnaround, 6 August 2026
position_start: Operating under the 1983 statute with an annual report to the trade minister and no stated efficiency target
position_end: The FY2024/25 annual report was submitted to the trade minister under section 40 of the Act, and in August 2026 the minister directed the body to cut certification turnaround for small and medium-sized enterprises and to rid the market of substandard products, rebalancing enforcement toward support. No turnaround figure, target or deadline is stated
note: the directive is a ministerial instruction with no instrument or measurable behind it

subject: gov.discourse
name: Climate information integrity project
milestone: Launched August 2026
position_end: A project on climate-change disinformation and information integrity in African digital ecosystems, focused on Uganda and Ethiopia and supported by a UNESCO-led global initiative, combining research mapping how climate disinformation spreads and who drives it with a fact-checking masterclass at the 2026 internet-freedom forum, online training for journalists and civil society, and tracking of African governments' communications ahead of the November 2026 climate conference
note: no budget or duration is stated

subject: gov.discourse
name: Fourth-cycle Universal Periodic Review
milestone: Joint civil-society submission filed, July 2026; review not yet held
position_start: Third-cycle review concluded January 2022 with 273 recommendations, 139 supported and 134 noted; no fourth-cycle submission on file (2025-08)
position_end: Joint submission by CIPESA, APC and WOUGNET filed, seeking repeal of the Computer Misuse Act speech offences, a statutory bar on network disruption, removal of the 12% excise duty on internet data, and statutory independence and fining powers for the Personal Data Protection Office; the review had not been held as at 2026-08-07
note: civil-society recommendations, not government commitments; the submission carries no day on its cover and the date is padded to the month

subject: gov.discourse
name: Judiciary media guidelines issued through ECCMIS
milestone: Revised guidelines issued through the case-management system for a High Court trial
position_end: Prior accreditation required, devices barred from the courtroom, live broadcasting granted case by case; the Law Society asked for the restrictions to be lifted
note: the guidelines themselves are not on file

subject: gov.discourse
name: URA e-Tax2 award
milestone: No work started as at July 2026 and no performance guarantee issued
position_start: Technical evaluation notice displayed 2025-08-25, under challenge
position_end: Award set aside by the Appeals Tribunal on a power-of-attorney defect, the capacity objection struck out unadjudicated; none of 26 commercial banks would issue the guarantee gating the 15% advance; joint-venture staff on the revenue authority's premises since January with no work started
note: the contract and evaluation report are not held; press allegations are recorded as allegations

subject: finance.budget
name: Domestic state digital-transformation budget
milestone: Vote 020 estimates published in the FY2026/27 ministerial policy statement
position_start: Not established; no vote-level figure for the programme was on the record
position_end: The ICT ministry's vote is financed domestically throughout the medium term, with external financing at nil in every year of the framework. The vote was approved at UGX 105.963bn for FY2025/26 excluding UGX 100.015bn of arrears, and is estimated at UGX 144.696bn for FY2026/27, rising to UGX 256.274bn by FY2030/31; the development half moves from UGX 0.574bn to UGX 46.426bn between those two years. Only UGX 40.566bn of the FY2025/26 vote had been spent by the end of December
note: the vote is the ministry's own and not the whole programme, which runs across several votes; the arrears line is larger than the substantive vote in FY2025/26 and is not explained in what is held

subject: finance.budget
name: National budget FY2026/27, science, technology and ICT allocation
milestone: Appropriation Bill adopted 24 April 2026
position_start: Did not exist for this financial year
position_end: Parliament passed a UGX 84.3 trillion budget on 24 April 2026, of which UGX 44.18 trillion is domestic revenue and UGX 11.27 trillion external project support; science, technology and innovation including ICT and the creative industry takes UGX 1.1 trillion, for innovation, digitisation of government services, internet expansion and business process outsourcing. Debt servicing at about UGX 33.4 trillion is close to 40 per cent of the whole
note: the UGX 1.1 trillion is a programme line covering more than digital transformation, and no split within it is published

subject: finance.mou
name: Ethio Telecom cooperation talks
milestone: Delegation visit to Addis Ababa, 2026-08-13
position_end: Preliminary: a ministerial delegation visited the Ethiopian incumbent's headquarters to explore cooperation on telecommunications infrastructure, digital payments, skills training and technology transfer in support of the national vision and the 2023-2027 digital roadmap; no agreement was signed
note: talks only; no scope, value or timetable is stated

subject: finance.new
name: Growth debt investment in a micro-enterprise lender
milestone: Debt investment recorded 2026
position_end: A US$2m growth debt investment by an innovation fund in a financial technology company lending to micro and small enterprises across Kenya and Uganda, on a model combining digital technology with in-person delivery; the investment is recorded as running from 2026 with no Ugandan portfolio split, disbursement schedule or borrower count published
note: the record is the investor's own project page; nothing states how much of it reaches Uganda

subject: finance.new
name: Uganda Digital Acceleration Project
milestone: Named as funder of three service-centre pilots
position_start: Active; free public Wi-Fi launched under it at the DRC border (2025-07-13)
position_end: Active; funding the Tororo, Mbarara and Gulu pilots, and named as the affordable-connectivity vehicle
note: World Bank US$200m, 2021-2027; no disbursement figure is held

subject: infra.connect
name: Active mobile subscriptions
milestone: UCC sector figure stated 2026-07-02
position_end: About 47m active SIMs (2026-07)
note: UCC states the figures come from licensees' own submissions

subject: infra.connect
name: Airtel Uganda customers and data use
milestone: Half-year results, six months to 2026-06-30
position_end: 19.7m customers at the half year to 30 June 2026, up 10%, of whom 8.9m are data customers, up 18.8%; data traffic rose 42.1% and average use per customer 21% to 7.2GB, with smartphone penetration at 46.6%
note: the operator's own half-year figures, carried in a trade account; no revenue, coverage or network figure accompanies them, and the base holds no comparable series for the second operator in the same period

subject: infra.connect
name: Bayobab Kampala-Malaba fibre route
milestone: Route lit, 260 km, over 1 Tbit/s
position_end: Unchanged; no capacity change or upgrade reported
note: in service before the window opened

subject: infra.connect
name: Border free public Wi-Fi, Bwera and Mpondwe
milestone: Launched on the DRC border
position_end: No expansion, usage figure or further site on record
note: launched two weeks before the window opened

subject: infra.connect
name: Census measures of individual ICT use
milestone: 2024 census final report published
position_end: Internet usage 2,809,327 persons or 8.9 per cent, 10.6 per cent of men and 7.6 per cent of women; mobile phone ownership among people aged 10 and above 31,389,721 or 43.3 per cent; fixed phone ownership 887,789 or 8.3 per cent; computer use in the last 30 days 1,224,199 or 3.9 per cent; use of online government services 639,188 or 2.0 per cent
note: a first national measurement on this definition, so no direction can be stated; it does not reconcile with the regulator's subscription-based count and no source compares them

subject: infra.connect
name: Framework on optical fibre installation, maintenance, protection and disposal
milestone: Effective 1 January 2026
position_end: In effect from 1 January 2026, setting minimum standards for deploying optical fibre cable infrastructure across the country and revising the rules governing its installation, maintenance, protection and disposal
note: issued by the communications regulator; no compliance, enforcement or deployment figure is on record against it

subject: infra.connect
name: MTN Uganda coverage and fibre footprint
milestone: Half-year results, six months to 2026-06-30
position_end: 25.4m mobile subscribers and 12.6m active data subscribers (2026-06-30); 96.2% 3G, 88.6% 4G and 19% 5G population coverage and 27,037 km fibre (2025-12-31)
note: company's own unaudited figures; the subscriber count was 24.2m at 2025-12-31 and the base holds no position at the window's opening

subject: infra.connect
name: National Backbone Infrastructure Phase V
milestone: Parliament approved an RMB 1.05bn loan 2023-12-06
position_start: Utilisation under 30% of full capacity; Phase V approved (2023-12)
position_end: No delivery, utilisation or completion figure published as at 2026-08-06
note: Service Uganda Centre throughput was made contingent on it

subject: infra.connect
name: National IP Peering Exchange
milestone: Launched at a workshop in Kampala, 17 April 2026
position_start: Did not exist; a peering policy was announced in October 2025

position_end: In service via Kigali, Kampala and Nairobi; Uganda partner Roke Telekom. The route was announced live and carrying traffic on 9 September 2026, alongside a Starlink launch in Uganda and a Layer 2 connectivity service over low-earth-orbit satellite for the East African market

subject: infra.connect

position_end: Approximately USD 1.40/GB for mobile data, attributed by EACO to a 40% tax burden on smartphones (EACO regional dataset, data period 2024-2025); UCC separately asserts costs continue to decline without publishing a figure (2026-07-02)

subject: infra.connect

milestone: 32 connected networks and about 40 Gbps peak through 2024

position_end: Unchanged in size: the exchange began and ended 2024 with 32 connected networks and about 40 Gbps of peak traffic, with churn either side. An endowment fund was launched to cover 25 per cent of annual non-salary operating expenses, a Netflix cache was deployed and an Akamai cache restored on contributed bandwidth, and free 100 Mbps ports are offered at the commercial Namanve facility with no cross-connect charge. A worldwide withdrawal of one content provider's remote peering depressed traffic mid-year
note: the operator's own annual report, and it names high taxes and a continuing social-media restriction as suppressing growth; no 2025 or 2026 figure is held

subject: infra.connect
name: Uganda-Tanzania fibre route on the transmission network
milestone: Procurement questioned by the parliamentary committee, 4 September 2026
position_end: The state transmission company cancelled an open bidding process for a commercialisation partner for its fibre network and moved to prepare a proposal for a single named company for the Uganda-Tanzania connection. The parliamentary committee on statutory authorities and state enterprises questioned why firms that had expressed interest were no longer being considered, in hearings on the Auditor General’s 2024/25 report. Documents before Parliament show the project rests on a presidential directive: a State House letter of 27 August 2025 told the ICT and energy ministers that a route through Tanzania could be cheaper than the existing route through Kenya, which the President described as full of commercial players looking for profit, and proposed carrying fibre on Tanzania’s high-voltage transmission line into the Ugandan transmission network (2026-09)
note: no contract, value, timetable or committee finding is held; the cost comparison between the two routes is the President’s assertion and is not evidenced in the account

subject: infra.store

position_end: Unchanged as a catalogue. Backup-as-a-service and disaster recovery are offered to government entities and other stakeholders alongside infrastructure as a service; no capacity, uptake, recovery-point or recovery-time figure is published for any of them

name: Rural electrification and last-mile connections

position_start: National electricity access at 51 per cent in 2020, 19 per cent on grid and 32 per cent off grid, with the access scale-up project running
position_end: Last-mile connections under the access scale-up project were commissioned district by district, Kiboga in August 2025, with free meters and free connection for anyone within 90 metres of a low voltage pole against fees of UGX 23,600 for inspection and UGX 6,400 for initial energy. The distribution company had taken on 850 additional connection technicians and, with the energy ministry, aims to connect at least 900,000 new customers by 2027 on US$638m of lender financing
note: the 2020 access figures are the energy policy's own and no later national rate is held; connections achieved under the project are not reported against the 900,000 target

subject: infra.capacity

position_start: Did not exist; agencies procured and managed their own security infrastructure
position_end: A centrally managed service introduced in February 2026 for every ministry, department and agency consuming the authority's IP and data-centre services, providing network protection without the agency procuring hardware or licences or managing security infrastructure of its own. No take-up count, price or coverage figure is published
note: announced to clients by circular; nothing records how many agencies have taken it

subject: infra.capacity

milestone: Assessed as a programme objective in the FY2023/24 budget monitoring report
position_start: No establishment, vacancy or workforce figure on the record
position_end: Still none. The finance ministry's own monitoring of the digital transformation programme treats a well-grounded ICT professional workforce as a distinct objective and reports against it, but no establishment figure, vacancy rate or attrition series for government ICT staff appears anywhere in this base
note: the absence is now dated and cited; the competence framework meant to define the roles was still at terms-of-reference stage at the close of the window

subject: infra.capacity
name: National IT Survey 2022
milestone: Third edition fielded January to April 2022
position_start: The third edition of the national survey of IT availability, access, usage, affordability and satisfaction, fielded across government and the public
position_end: Unchanged and not repeated. The survey sampled 132 ministries, departments and agencies, 128 districts, 3,960 households and individuals and 600 businesses between January and April 2022, developed with the statistics bureau, and remains the only empirical measurement in this base of what government and local government actually run on. No fourth edition is on record four years on
note: the capture is truncated mid-report, so the survey's findings are not carried into this base - only its scope and sample

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Central bank internal security systems
milestone: Governor told Parliament the systems were strengthened
position_end: Internal security systems strengthened after a physical break-in and allegations of system manipulation at the central bank's headquarters, the governor telling Parliament's Public Accounts Committee that the incidents involved a physical security breach and fraudulent payments rather than an external cyberattack and that any perceived weaknesses had been addressed
note: no incident report, loss figure or independent assessment is on record

subject: infra.cybersec

milestone: Target date restated as March 2027, reported 2026-08-27
position_end: Originally due earlier and now targeted for March 2027. The criminal investigations directorate told a parliamentary committee inspection that it will recruit internally to close an investigator shortage and wants government and security databases integrated so detectives can link suspects, incidents and evidence quickly, its director saying integration would first require agreement on the legal and policy frameworks governing access
note: no budget, site or build stage for the centre is stated, and the original due date is not given

position_end: Guidelines launched on 8 June 2026 introduce compliance requirements and sanctions for education officials and institutions that fail to meet data-management obligations, make registration on the system mandatory for every school, and confirm that capitation grants and resource allocation are determined from the system's data. Every learner carries a unique learner identification number, and institutions must submit location, ownership status and governance structure
note: the guidelines document is not held; the system was redeveloped in July 2022 to replace the annual school census and the ministry's own account names stakeholder mistrust and misdeclaration as continuing problems

note: no conformance, adoption or connected-system count against the guidelines is published

subject: dpi.exchange

Enforcement runs at all border points, with the firm's staff deployed under South Sudan Revenue Authority cover; the Tanzanian and Rwandan revenue authorities have publicly dissociated themselves from the scheme
note: enforcement of a third country's charge, run on the customs platform; an amendment act of September 2025 gives electronic customs records their legal basis and a regional customs bond piloted from August 2025 sits alongside it

position_end: The registration authority's own account describes the secure identification system carrying a birth and death registration module, with a national identification number issued automatically on birth notification and certification following immediately. A technical working group on civil registration and vital statistics adopted a health-facility death process map in April 2026 and data-sharing arrangements with the statistics bureau
note: the architecture is presented rather than evaluated: no share of births actually notified electronically, and no time-to-certificate figure, is published

subject: dpi.id

position_start: 2014-15 cards expiring end-2025; 100,000 enhanced cards printed (2025-07-16)
position_end: Laser-engraved cards with QR and barcode, ghost image and digital signature in all districts and diaspora issuance opened in Dubai in February 2026 — but the QR codes on newly issued cards do not work, which the registration authority acknowledged publicly on 9 February 2026 and which was raised in Parliament on 20 August: banks turning citizens away, telecoms unable to verify SIM applications, and a Shs5,000 charge for a workaround letter
note: the failure has stood since at least February 2026 with no published fix date and no count of affected cards; Parliament's own record of the sitting has the registration authority acknowledging on 9 February 2026 that QR functionality had not been integrated into its digital operational system and promising a fix by 31 March 2026, and the Government Chief Whip undertaking that the internal affairs minister would respond

position_end: Still not working nearly five months after that deadline. Members of parliament reported on 20 August 2026 that holders of newly issued cards were being turned away from banking services and from buying or replacing SIM cards because the codes were not responding, and raised an additional UGX 5,000 charge for a letter enabling a citizen whose card cannot be verified electronically to have their details integrated. The government undertook to seek a response from the internal affairs minister

subject: dpi.id

position_end: The revenue authority and the identification authority are migrating the tax identification number onto the national identification number, to establish a single identity framework across identity, taxation and public administration. A published analysis describes the reform as one of the most significant administrative changes of recent years and sets its benefits against risks of concentrating identity, tax and administrative records on one identifier. Both authorities have since described the work as interoperability between two identifiers rather than the abolition of one, with the identification number the single index and the taxpayer number retained (2026-09)
