note: no premium, policy-count or target published

subject: dpi.pay
name: AKIBA tokenised-asset exchange
milestone: A majority-stake acquisition moved on 2026-04-08
position_end: A regulated tokenised-asset exchange to run under the central-bank and capital-markets sandboxes; no licence, launch date or volume published

subject: dpi.pay
name: Cash-withdrawal caps
milestone: Circular issued 2026-05-29, effective 2027-01-01
position_end: Over-the-counter withdrawals capped at UGX 50m a day and 250m a week for individuals, UGX 500m a day and 2.5bn a week for businesses; interbank cheque limits halved
note: the stated purpose is a cash-lite economy

subject: dpi.pay
name: Cashless fare collection on an electric bus route
milestone: Route launched in Kira Municipality, 2026-08-28
position_end: An operator and an electric bus company launched a route in Kira Municipality carrying cashless fare collection, presented as combining electric mobility, connectivity and digital payments; the launch was attended by the minister for science, technology and innovation in the Office of the President and the minister for Kampala Capital City. No fleet size, fare, ridership, payment instrument or route length is published
note: a launch announcement carried in a trade account; it is the base's first instance of fare collection on a public transport route being digitised, which is why it is carried at all

subject: dpi.pay
name: Centenary and MicroPay platform memorandum
milestone: Memorandum signed at Mapeera House, reported 2026-07-24
position_end: Intent to build school-fees saving and instalment payment with payment-history-based financing, agent-network healthcare payments and digitised insurance; no amount, launch date, user target or governance arrangement
note: the signature date is unestablished, and nothing is on file about consent, retention or legal basis for the credit-scoring layer

subject: dpi.pay
name: Digital shilling CBDC pilot
milestone: Announced within a US$5.5bn settlement-network plan, 2025-10-08
position_end: A bond-backed pilot tied to a special economic zone, financed by tokenised loans; the central bank separately records a CBDC study as planned, and its own stakeholder consultations report 83.4 per cent of Ugandans trusting a central bank digital currency as a safe way to pay and nearly 79 per cent preferring it to cash. No pilot design, date or participant is on record
note: the trust and preference figures are the central bank's own consultation, with no sample size, method or fieldwork date published beside them

subject: dpi.pay
name: Direct yuan settlement through CIPS
milestone: Opened for Ugandan businesses, reported 2026-08-07
position_end: A commercial bank has opened direct yuan settlement for Ugandan businesses trading with China by integrating China's Cross-Border Interbank Payment System, cutting reliance on the dollar leg; Uganda imported US$3.3bn from China in 2025 against US$118m of exports
note: one bank's service rather than a national rail; no volume, fee or central-bank position is stated

subject: dpi.pay
name: E-money transaction value
milestone: Central-bank FY2024/25 figures, reported 2025-10-06
position_start: FY2023/24 value not separately held; growth reported at 28.6%
position_end: UGX 326tn in FY2024/25; agent banking UGX 29.4tn, up 76.1%, and agents 22,793, up 49.1%, while debit-card use fell 5.1% to 3.6m and internet-banking users fell 6.6% to 0.9m
sources: 2025-10-06 BoU's New Payment System Cuts Delays and Boosts E-Money by 28.6%
note: growth is in agents and handsets; both screen-based channels contracted

subject: dpi.pay
name: EACBond regional customs guarantee
milestone: Launched in Kampala with Uganda as a pilot country, 4 August 2025
position_start: Did not exist; traders secured multiple national bonds
position_end: Launched as a regional customs guarantee instrument replacing the need for separate national bonds when moving goods across partner states, allowing a trader to secure an entire cargo once. Uganda is a pilot country. No uptake, value guaranteed or participating-institution count is published
note: launched by the Community secretariat; nothing records the Ugandan pilot's start, scope or results

subject: dpi.pay
name: Feasibility study of government payment mechanisms for social protection
milestone: Published by the gender ministry, November 2023
position_start: Published as the government's own assessment of which platforms could carry social-protection payments, naming the financial management system, a bank-connect channel and an electronic cash mechanism as candidates
position_end: Unchanged as a study. Nothing in the base records a decision taken on its recommendations, a platform selected, or a programme migrated onto one; the payments that did move went through the parish programme's own account infrastructure instead
note: three years on with no recorded decision, which is the finding rather than the study's content

subject: dpi.pay
name: Interbank settlement, clearing and shared agent banking platforms
milestone: Central bank figures for the year to June 2025
position_start: Values for the year to June 2024: settlement system UGX 808.7tn, electronic funds transfers UGX 59.4tn, agent banking UGX 16.7tn, cheques UGX 4.8tn
position_end: Year to June 2025: the interbank settlement system carried UGX 955.6tn on 2.5 million transactions, up 18.2 per cent in value and 21.8 per cent in volume; electronic funds transfers UGX 64.6tn on 13.7 million transactions, up 8.7 per cent; the shared agent banking platform UGX 29.4tn on 12.5 million transactions, up 76.1 per cent in value and 50.5 per cent in volume, with 24 institutions signed up; cheque values fell 3.6 per cent to UGX 4.6tn and cheques were 6.2 per cent of volume against 6.9 per cent a year earlier
note: the cheque decline follows a cap on interbank cheques in force since January 2022; the central bank states it may lower the cap further

subject: dpi.pay
name: Kampala-Entebbe Expressway toll collection
milestone: Parliamentary committee report presented 2026-08-25
position_end: The concession remains reliant on cash transactions. A parliamentary infrastructure committee recommended on 25 August 2026 that the revenue authority take over collection and introduce an electronic payment system, called for a forensic audit of the concession's operations and revenue collections, and asked for scrutiny of a reported UGX 36 billion one-year extension of a security contract; the ICT minister of state told the House that the operator has never given government the source code or password of the system
note: the Speaker ruled that the recommendations be considered by the whole House on 27 August 2026; no decision is held

subject: dpi.pay
name: Mobile money platform migration to a cloud-native vendor platform
milestone: Migration completed across four markets, reported 2026-08-21
position_end: The dominant operator's mobile money platform moved off a legacy virtualised environment onto a cloud-native vendor fintech platform, the vendor reporting cuts of up to 86% in CPU processing and database load and up to 80% in API response times; the migration completed in Eswatini, Ghana, Rwanda and Uganda, with Cameroon under way and Benin, the Republic of the Congo and Zambia in discussion
note: the performance figures are the vendor's own; no downtime, cost or subscriber-impact figure is stated

subject: dpi.pay
name: MTN MoMo active users
milestone: 2025 sustainability report, published 2026-08-05
position_start: More than 10m active users, over UGX 55tn a year (2025-07-23)
position_end: 14.7m active subscribers; more than 5bn transactions worth UGX 195.5tn; 241,000 active agents and 114,800 merchants
note: the two transaction-value figures are not reconcilable and no growth rate is derived from them

subject: dpi.pay
name: MTN MoMo separation and listing
milestone: Shareholders approved separation into a new financial company, 2025-07-23
position_start: Separation approved, a listing under consideration (2025-07-23)
position_end: Unchanged; no listing, completion or revised timetable on record as at 2026-08-06

subject: dpi.pay
name: National Payment Switch
milestone: Reported in progress in the central bank's FY2024/25 account
position_end: Unchanged; nothing further held as at 2026-08-06
sources: 2025-10-06 BoU's New Payment System Cuts Delays and Boosts E-Money by 28.6%

subject: dpi.pay
name: Non-tax revenue collection through the revenue authority's digital interface
milestone: Consolidated collection mandate stated by the revenue authority
position_start: In service: fees previously collected by individual ministries, departments and agencies are collected and accounted for centrally by the revenue authority through its electronic tax and payment reference number interface
position_end: Unchanged. The authority states it does not provide the underlying services but collects and accounts for the fees; no non-tax revenue total, channel split or agency count is published in what is held
note: a standing service description rather than a performance record

subject: dpi.pay
name: Okusevinga USSD micro-investing pilot
milestone: Reported as a 2026 pilot in a comparative account, 2026-07-31
position_end: USSD access to money-market and bond funds from UGX 10,000, intended to draw cash and informal savings-group money into regulated instruments; no provider, launch date or user figure published
note: reported only as a comparator in a Lesotho-led piece surveying wallet-based micro-investing across East and southern Africa; no primary Ugandan source, provider name or launch date held

subject: dpi.pay
name: PAPSS participation
milestone: United Bank for Africa's Uganda subsidiary announced live on the rail 2026-08-03
position_end: One commercial bank live, announced by the operator with no go-live date distinct from the announcement, no corridor list, no volumes and no tariff; no held source puts the Bank of Uganda on the system as a settlement participant

subject: dpi.pay
name: RTGS replacement and ISO 20022 migration
milestone: Go-live stated for November 2025
movement: No change, target date passed unverified
position_end: Unchanged; no held source confirms or denies go-live
sources: 2025-10-06 BoU's New Payment System Cuts Delays and Boosts E-Money by 28.6%
note: absence of confirmation is not evidence of non-delivery

subject: dpi.pay
name: SCRYPT stablecoin settlement corridor
milestone: Corridor opened, reported 2026-07-16
position_end: A licensed local-currency-in, stablecoin-out settlement corridor across four East African markets including Uganda; no volume or counterparty figure published

subject: dpi.pay
name: Smartlife Flexi voluntary savings over mobile money
milestone: Partnership renewed, reported 2026-08-31
position_start: Running as a partnership between the national social security fund and a mobile-money operator
position_end: Renewed, letting savers contribute from UGX 500 by mobile phone from any location
note: a renewal announcement; no subscriber count, balance or contribution volume is published, and the original term is not stated

subject: dpi.pay
name: Tax payment on MTN MoMo
milestone: Enhanced tax and government payment menu live nationwide, December 2025
position_end: Free USSD tax payment on any handset; the revenue authority collected UGX 15.25tn net in H1 FY2025/26 against a UGX 14.93tn target. The operator and the authority put an enhanced tax and government payment menu live nationwide on a dedicated shortcode in December 2025, and in March 2026 the operator removed transaction fees on all payments below UGX 5,000
sources: 2026-03-30-mtn-momo-power-of-momo-campaign|2025-12-23-mtn-momo-ura-enhance-digital-tax-services|2025-12-23 URA Launches Enhanced Tax Payment Services on MTN MoMo to Boost Digital Compliance
note: the fee removal is one operator's commercial campaign, not a regulated tariff, and no duration or transaction-volume effect is published

subject: dpi.pay
name: UnionPay e-commerce acceptance
milestone: Extended to nine African markets 2026-08-19
position_start: A Standard Bank and UnionPay collaboration since 2024, with no online acceptance on record
position_end: Online acceptance open to participating merchants, settling in local currency, US dollars or both
note: nearly 900 participating merchants across the nine markets, and about 7 million UnionPay cards issued in Africa, are the two companies' own figures; no country-specific count is given

subject: dpi.registry
name: Alien registration and Alien Identification Number
milestone: First Alien ID cards issued (2026-08); 1,875 enrolled since 2026-06-10
position_end: First cards issued, with 1,875 foreigners enrolled in the ten weeks since registration opened, against about 2m registered foreigners in scope; the US$100 card is required for SIM registration, banking and business access but confers no vote
note: about 1.95m of those in scope are refugees or asylum-seekers, so enrolment of 1,875 in ten weeks is under a tenth of a percent of the scope, and the US$100 fee falls on a population overwhelmingly composed of refugees. Nothing is published about a waiver, an instalment route or what happens to a resident foreigner who cannot pay yet needs a SIM or a bank account

subject: dpi.registry
name: Birth registration drive
milestone: Community drives and a fee schedule announced 2026-06-01
position_start: Registration system in 112 of 135 districts and 222 of 5,230 birth-handling facilities (2020); certificate holding 32% (2016)
position_end: Community drives of ten or more parents; under-nine-months exempt from biometrics; certificates free under six months then UGX 10,000, 20,000 and 50,000 by age band. Registration teams were deployed to referral hospitals during the mass enrolment exercise to register births and issue identification numbers on the spot, and 636,000 children had been enrolled by January 2026
sources: 2026-06-01-nira-birth-registration-alien-registration|2026-01-07-monitor-21-million-transferred-new-nira-system|2025-09-29-nira-instant-birth-registrations|2020-01-01 Maintaining civil registration amid COVID-19 - Uganda's mobile notification system (IDRC)
note: no birth-registration coverage figure published since 2016, so the 636,000 cannot be read against a denominator

subject: dpi.registry
name: Digital number plate system
milestone: Parliamentary committee inquiry opened
position_start: Issuing at about 350 plates a day
position_end: Daily production has fallen to about 100 plates from roughly 350, with a widening backlog; a parliamentary infrastructure committee opened a fact-finding inquiry on 2 September 2026 after complaints from vehicle dealers about shortages, administrative delay and cost, and members put the loss to the economy at more than 4bn shillings a week against a first-registration fee of 714,300 shillings (2026-09)
note: the weekly loss figure is legislators' own estimate, not an audited or agency figure, and the operator has published no account of the shortfall

subject: dpi.registry
name: Land registry digitisation
milestone: Lands ministry statement of intent, reported 2026-04-07
position_end: Blockchain and artificial-intelligence systems planned to cut transaction fraud, plus mass titling; no procurement, budget, supplier or date. Separately the land commission announced in March 2026 a nationwide geographic-information-based digital registry of government-owned land, to counter encroachment and raise revenue, also without procurement, budget or date
note: two separate announcements of digital land registration in a month, from different bodies and covering different land, and nothing on file relates them

subject: dpi.registry
name: Marriage registration under NIRA
milestone: Transferred from the registration bureau, April 2025
position_start: Births, marriages and deaths under one body (2025-04)
position_end: Unchanged
note: the transfer closed three months before the window opened

subject: dpi.registry
name: National addressing and postcode database
milestone: Postcodes geo-referenced for 27 central districts, FY2025/26
position_start: Under development as a vote output, with coverage stated at 10 per cent against a 20 per cent target for FY2025/26
position_end: A geo-referenced postcode database was built for all parishes and wards in 27 districts of central Uganda during FY2025/26, and an addressing pilot at Entebbe assigned standard addresses, with lessons to be documented before national expansion. No national coverage figure, completion date or address count is published
note: the 10 and 20 per cent figures are vote-output targets whose denominator the statement does not define

subject: dpi.registry
name: National Single Registry for social protection
milestone: Operationalisation still a stated systems priority, 2026-2030 country plan
position_start: In service as the unified platform holding information across social protection programmes, premised on linking programme management systems and the national identity database
position_end: Five years after launch the base holds no statement of coverage, linked programmes or records held. A donor country plan approved in October 2025 for 2026 to 2030 records operationalising the registry as a continuing systems priority, and the 2025 country report records continued support for integrating a sub-national social registry into it - so it is described as work still to be done rather than a platform in service
note: both accounts of its incompleteness are a donor's rather than the responsible ministry's, which has published nothing operational about it since the launch

subject: dpi.registry
name: National Voters Register and biometric verification
status: Implemented, verification unreliable on the day
milestone: Fallback to the printed register directed on polling day, 15 January 2026
position_start: Compiled and maintained by the electoral commission under its exclusive constitutional mandate, with biometric verification not yet compulsory
position_end: A statutory instrument signed in December 2025 made use of the biometric voter verification kit compulsory at every polling station for the 2026 general elections. On polling day the commission issued guidance that where a kit failed to start, voting should begin immediately using the printed National Voters Register - so the fallback to paper was the operating position on the day the requirement first bit
note: no count of kits that failed, stations affected or voters verified biometrically is published; the commission's own December statement warns that unauthorised hosting or distribution of voter registration data is an offence

subject: dpi.registry
name: Registration of Titles Act and the Register Book
milestone: Consolidated text as at 31 December 2023
position_start: In force as the statutory basis of the land register, requiring a registrar of titles and a register book in which certificates of title are recorded
position_end: Unchanged as the legal basis. What moved is administration rather than statute: 44,425 freehold titles were handed to landowners across 13 districts under a systematic titling programme from August 2025, and the land commission announced a nationwide geographic-information-based digital registry of government-owned land in March 2026 to counter encroachment and raise revenue
note: the digital registry covers government land only; no procurement, supplier, budget or date is on record for it, and no national count of titled parcels is held

subject: dpi.registry
name: Sugar Industry Information Management System
milestone: Launched at the trade ministry, reported 2026-09-03
position_end: Built by the trade, industry and cooperatives ministry with the National Sugar Stakeholders Council to register every sugarcane farmer in the country and centralise data across the value chain - cane cultivation, harvesting, milling, processing, distribution and market trends - in one view of the industry
note: no farmer count, registration deadline, cost, vendor or data-protection provision is published, and nothing states how it relates to the national identification register

subject: dpi.registry
name: Taxpayer register and its identifier
milestone: Mandatory update of registration details, effective 1 July 2025
position_start: Maintained under the value added tax statute's requirement that the commissioner general keep a register of all taxable persons, on a tax identification number of its own
position_end: The identifier is being replaced: section 4 of the tax procedures code requires the tax identification number to give way to the national identification number for individuals or the business registration number for entities from 1 July 2025, and the revenue authority has notified every registered taxpayer to update their registration details, with portal access controlled on that basis. A unified identifier merging all three across the revenue, identity and business registries is under consideration
note: no count of taxpayers updated, nor any deadline or sanction for those who have not, is published; the consolidated tax statute on file carries outstanding amendments not applied

subject: dpi.registry
name: URSB Non-Individual Register
milestone: Financial-year stakeholder engagements opened, August 2026
position_end: A centralised digital register for companies, partnerships, NGOs, cooperatives and community organisations, each given a unique entity registration number; the registry opened its 2026/27 stakeholder engagements in August 2026
note: the corporate counterpart to the national ID number; no registered-entity count published

subject: dpi.mis
name: AI-assisted febrile-illness surveillance in the community health information system
milestone: Phase II opened, workers now shown the model's interpretation
position_end: An artificial-intelligence-assisted febrile-illness surveillance workflow built into the electronic community health information system recorded high agreement with village health teams' unaided judgments in a first phase, and enters a three-month second phase in which workers are shown the model's interpretation. It runs in four districts, implemented by the health ministry with a non-governmental technology organisation using a third party's diagnostic interpreter
note: no agreement percentage, sample size or case count has been published, so the headline finding cannot be checked; the first phase itself logged low testing volumes, inconsistent commodity availability, device underperformance, unreliable connectivity and supervision gaps

subject: dpi.mis
name: ASYCUDA World customs system
milestone: Described by the revenue authority as the operational customs system
position_start: In service for processing all imports and exports, with self-declaration, assessment and payment by the trader and commercial documents attachable online
position_end: Unchanged as the platform. What moved around it is legal and regional: an amendment act recognising electronic records in customs documentation, and a regional customs bond launched with Uganda as a pilot country
note: no declaration volume, clearance time or availability figure is published for the system

subject: dpi.mis
name: E-Ward Round remote specialist platform
milestone: Launched 2026-09-03
position_end: A private digital-health company launched a platform on 3 September 2026 letting urban specialists run virtual multidisciplinary ward rounds with rural inpatient teams in real time, with per-bed cryptographic tokens and artificial-intelligence triage on live vital signs; the company says 67% of its partner facilities have inpatient capacity, covering more than 260 medical wards that often lack cardiologists, neurologists and intensivists (2026-09)
note: a commercial launch: no facility list, patient volume, tariff, clinical evaluation or integration with the national health information stack is published

subject: dpi.mis
name: Education management information system (Education DHIS2 and the School Report Card)
status: Implemented, governed by guidelines since June 2026
milestone: Data-governance guidelines launched 8 June 2026
position_end: Multiple unaligned systems fragmented education information management and the absence of a formal policy was named as a cause of limited accountability and weak data culture in schools. Guidelines launched on 8 June 2026 close that gap: compliance requirements and sanctions for officials and institutions, mandatory registration for every school, a unique learner identification number, and capitation grants determined from the system's data
note: the guidelines document is not held, and the ministry's own account names stakeholder mistrust and misdeclaration of information as continuing problems

subject: dpi.mis
name: Handover of donor-built digital health systems to the health ministry
milestone: Assets transferred 31 March 2026
position_start: Built and run by a university programme outside the ministry
position_end: Digital health systems described as worth US$100m were transferred from a university programme to the health ministry on 31 March 2026, among them the health information exchange platform, the electronic medical records repositories, disease-surveillance trackers and stock-status and quality-improvement systems. The programme's own record of what it built includes a functional national data warehouse, 1,300 facilities running case-based surveillance and 1,084 running recency surveillance
note: the US$100m is the university's own valuation of the assets, not a transaction price, and no ministry running-cost or staffing plan for them is published

subject: dpi.mis
name: Health management information system
milestone: Newborn-data functionality assessed across 53 data offices in four countries
position_end: DHIS2 is the routine electronic health information system, with functionality for generating facility annual summary reports available in every data office assessed
note: a cross-sectional study run between November 2022 and July 2024; no national coverage or maturity figure is held

subject: dpi.mis
name: KIX-SEEDS education data systems project
milestone: Issue brief published December 2025
position_end: A GPE/KIX-funded project coordinated by APHRC with HISP Uganda, ESEA Senegal and ISSP Burkina Faso as country implementing partners, working on sub-national education-data collection, quality and use; a year of work was reviewed at the Ouagadougou annual general meeting of June 2025 and an issue brief published in December 2025. No budget, end date or coverage figure is on the record
note: Runs across Uganda, Senegal and Burkina Faso together.

subject: dpi.mis
name: National Laboratory Data Repository
milestone: Launched 2026-02-05
position_end: A one-stop platform linking laboratory information systems to the National Health Data Warehouse for real-time surveillance and planning
note: extends the existing health-information stack

subject: dpi.mis
name: National Shock Responsive Social Protection Framework
milestone: Issued by the gender ministry, February 2025
position_start: Did not exist on the record
position_end: Issued as the framework for responding to disasters and shocks through the social protection system, defining the single and social registries and naming beneficiary registration as a continuing systems challenge. No activation, trigger or payout under it is recorded
note: the framework names the registry weakness that the registry row records, from the responsible ministry's own hand

subject: dpi.mis
name: Northern Uganda Social Action Fund IV and the dynamic social registry
milestone: Launch stated to be imminent, June 2026
position_start: Not on the record as a funded vehicle
position_end: Carried in the FY2026/27 public investment plan as a project of the prime minister's office with funding allocated, and named as the vehicle for operationalising a dynamic national social registry; the permanent secretary stated in June 2026 that it would be launched soon. No launch date, budget figure or registry design is on record
note: the registry it is meant to operationalise was launched in 2021 and has no operational record since, so this is a second attempt at the same object

subject: dpi.mis
name: Parish Development Model Information System
milestone: Household coverage and disbursement tracking stated, August 2025
position_end: The system captures beneficiary names, national identification numbers, telephone numbers, locations, enterprises, business plans, borrowed amounts, repayments, savings and cooperative affiliations, covering nearly 79 per cent of all households in the country; in just over two years it is tracking more than UGX 2.7 trillion sent to programme cooperatives, of which UGX 2.5 trillion reached more than 2.5 million beneficiaries. Access is restricted to named implementing institutions
note: the account is the ICT ministry's own; no audit, error rate or grievance figure is published, and the remaining fifth of households is not quantified

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Civil-society partnership on contract monitoring
milestone: Partnership announced by the procurement authority, August 2026
position_end: The public procurement and disposal authority has partnered with a budget-advocacy group to strengthen monitoring of government contracts; no scope, dataset or first published finding is on file

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Copyright Management System
milestone: September 2026 rollout targeted, testing under way (2026-08)
position_end: In testing, with a September 2026 rollout targeted
note: announced by the justice minister with the registration services bureau supporting implementation alongside collective management organisations; no cost, supplier, rights-holder count or description of what the system registers or pays out is published, and the target date is the only dated commitment held

subject: dpi.govtech
name: East African digital public infrastructure project pipeline
milestone: Consultancy tendered 2026-08-05
position_end: German-funded consultancy tendered to identify and prepare bankable digital public infrastructure projects across Uganda, Kenya and Tanzania, covering digital identity, data exchange, payments and e-government; value, duration and selected consultant not stated
note: under the EU-East African Community programme; the record is a procurement notice, so it fixes the consultancy stage and nothing about any project it may prepare

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Electronic Government Procurement system
milestone: Training opened for 100 further entities, 2026-08-03
position_end: 136 entities onboarded and Version 2.0 in service, verifying suppliers automatically against URA, URSB, NIRA and NSSF records; onboarded entities no longer advertise tenders in newspapers and may transact only with registered providers. The finance minister put the system alongside budget-execution controls and the accounting profession's own role in evidence-based decision-making at a professional seminar on 3 September 2026, without new figures for onboarding or throughput (2026-09)
note: the start figure carries no date; PPDA states onboarding continues each financial year until all of government is on the system

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Government Procurement Portal
milestone: 36 of 78 candidate data points selected and validated, December 2025
position_start: Publishing machine-readable procurement data, with no project-level or safeguard data
position_end: 36 of 78 candidate data points across social, institutional, environmental, economic and climate-finance dimensions were selected and validated with the procuring entities by December 2025, against a decline in infrastructure data disclosure the project was set up to reverse; inputs from the finance ministry, the works ministry and the civil aviation authority were still outstanding, and no go-live, completion or published dataset is recorded
note: the work is run by a transparency initiative and a freedom-of-information centre on the procurement authority's behalf, and the account is theirs

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Human Rights Commission case-management system
milestone: Launched 2026-08-12 under the government network programme
position_end: Launched by the national IT authority alongside the teacher-training platform, digitising the Human Rights Commission’s case handling; no caseload, retention rule or data-protection assessment is published for a system holding complaint records

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Mandatory electronic invoicing
milestone: Phased rollout mandated by revenue-authority public notice of 2026-08-10
position_start: Did not exist; the statutory basis was put in place by the Tax Procedures Code (Amendment) Act 2025, gazetted 4 July 2025, which substitutes section 4 of the Tax Procedures Code
position_end: Mandatory in a phased, sector-specific rollout: immediately for businesses registered for value-added tax, which captures enterprises above an annual turnover of Ush300m (about US$80,864), and immediately for named high-risk and high-value sectors - manufacturing, mining and quarrying, construction, wholesale and retail, and others. A bill gazetted on 27 March 2026 revises the penal tax for failure to use an electronic fiscal device or to issue an electronic invoice or receipt
note: the bill is gazetted rather than passed on this record, and the revised penalty amounts are not extracted here

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Police artificial-intelligence chatbot
milestone: Announced at the police ICT facility
position_end: The police force is to introduce an artificial-intelligence chatbot to help the public reach police services and information, giving guidance on how to respond to emergencies, where to seek assistance and how to obtain information on services offered
note: announced on a visit to the police ICT facility with no launch date, model, vendor, language coverage or data-handling statement, and no account of how a chatbot's guidance on emergencies would be assured

subject: dpi.govtech
name: U-Learn teacher-training platform
milestone: Launched 2026-08-12 under the government network programme
position_end: Launched by the national IT authority as one of two new e-services under the government network programme, with more than 6,600 teachers enrolled at launch; no curriculum, completion rate or running cost is published

subject: digital.localgov
name: Backbone fibre extension to district and sub-county offices
milestone: Kanungu district connected December 2025; Kampala ducting under way
position_start: District and sub-county offices connected where the backbone reached, with no district-level programme on the record
position_end: The backbone's fifth phase was extended to Kanungu district in December 2025, connecting district and sub-county local-government offices, in a collaboration between the IT authority, the president's office and the ICT ministry. In the Greater Kampala metropolitan area overhead fibre is being relocated into shared underground ducts across the local authorities. No count of local governments connected, nor a target, is published
note: district-by-district accounts with no national denominator behind them

subject: digital.localgov
name: Electronic document and records management in local governments
milestone: Training and onboarding at two district local governments, 17 August 2026
position_start: Deployed at central user agencies and listed as a vote output, with local government named only as a connectivity priority
position_end: The records-management system reached district level in August 2026 with training and onboarding at two district local governments. subject: data.satellite
name: ClimCam Earth-observation payload
milestone: Launched to the International Space Station, 8 April 2026
position_start: Did not exist; no Ugandan Earth-observation instrument in orbit
position_end: A climate camera payload built with the Egyptian and Kenyan space agencies was launched on 8 April 2026 aboard a resupply mission and installed on a commercial platform attached to the station's European module, after assembly and testing in Cairo and validation in Houston. It is to deliver near-real-time weather and climate data for disaster management, natural resource planning and climate resilience across eastern Africa, and was selected under an initiative led by the United Nations outer space office with an aerospace manufacturer
note: a shared regional payload rather than a national satellite; no data-access arrangement, ground-segment or Ugandan user is named

subject: data.satellite
name: Meteorological use of satellite-derived data
milestone: Satellite-derived datasets recorded in operational use, hydromet diagnostic 2024
position_start: In operational use at the meteorological authority, on a legal basis established by its 2012 statute, as recorded in an independently peer-reviewed diagnostic
position_end: Unchanged in the diagnostic record. What has moved is upstream rather than in the forecasting office: a regional Earth-observation payload reached orbit in April 2026 whose data is intended for climate and disaster use across eastern Africa, with no arrangement stated for how the meteorological authority would receive or use it
note: the diagnostic is a donor-facility peer review; no observation-network density, forecast skill or warning-coverage figure is carried into this base

subject: data.satellite
name: Satellite and sensor monitoring in agriculture
milestone: Field monitoring station deployed at a Mayuge farm, August 2026
position_start: Provided for as a funded subcomponent of the climate-smart agriculture project, with no deployment on the record
position_end: Two pilots are running and neither is a national service. A European Space Agency demonstration supporting sugarcane growers and millers completed monitoring trials, on the stated problem that yields run at about 40 per cent of potential; and a field monitoring station was deployed at a farm in Mayuge district in August 2026 for real-time environmental data and later integration with European Earth-observation data. The state's own instrument is the climate-smart agricultural transformation project, whose subcomponent funds satellite-based agro-climatic information partnerships under a US$325m credit and a US$25m equivalent grant
note: both deployments are single-site and privately or donor led; nothing records a national agricultural Earth-observation service or a farmer-reached figure

subject: geopol.usa
name: United States health-data access agreement
milestone: Signed at Kampala 2025-12-10 for activities running 2026-04-01 to 2030-12-31
position_end: The signed memorandum caps the data-sharing arrangement at seven years from execution, places it under joint steering-committee governance with the Government of Uganda as data owner, requires prior written authorisation through a Data Sharing Agreement approved by both, binds all data activities to the Data Protection and Privacy Act Cap 97 and the National Data Governance Framework, and has Uganda approve the national health information architecture before any United States-financed investment; planned United States support is US$1,719,960,000 against Uganda's US$577,001,796, including US$113,102,289 for data systems. The MOU only provides for a future Data Sharing Agreement (§2.5.2); ProPublica reported 2026-07-23 that it reviewed that agreement directly and that it grants direct, real-time login access to nine of Uganda's health data systems for seven years, a term matching the MOU's own cap. The agreement's text is unpublished and not held, and no Ugandan or US primary has confirmed or denied ProPublica's account (reconciled 2026-08-10) Eight United States senators wrote to the Secretary of State in the week to 2026-08-19 challenging the arrangement, noting that the Uganda agreement provides up to US$1.7bn in aid for HIV, tuberculosis and malaria among other diseases against direct access to the government's own health data systems, and requesting a briefing and a written answer by the end of August 2026.
note: the signed memorandum is now held and only provides for a future Data Sharing Agreement (§2.5.2); ProPublica says it reviewed that agreement directly and describes direct, real-time access to nine systems for seven years — the two accounts describe different instruments, not a conflict (reconciled 2026-08-10)

subject: geopol.india

milestone: Joint statement issued on the state visit of 24-25 July 2018
position_end: The joint statement issued on the Indian prime minister's state visit of 24 to 25 July 2018 - the first such visit in twenty-one years - is the founding modern instrument, carrying four memoranda alongside lines of credit and grants, a joint commitment to collaboration in information and communications technology, and Uganda's stated intent to replicate Indian digital inclusion schemes while implementing its own public key infrastructure project.
